tier.description: Lowercase tier code the license names, or `"community"` when absent.

key.description: The closed-vocabulary feature key (lowercase kebab-case slug; the same string the gate attribute carries).

available.description: True when the current bool IEdition.Has(Feature feature) covers this key.

items.description:
One feature's availability at the current edition. The view is honest
about every entry — including paid keys under Community, where
`available` is `false` — so the dashboard can render the
right disabled/locked affordance without a second call to the catalog.

features.description: Every registered feature, with `available` reflecting the current edition.

key.description: The closed-vocabulary limit key (lowercase kebab-case slug; the same string the gate attribute carries).

current.description: Currently-observed usage (best-effort from the matching provider, or 0).

cap.description: Effective numeric cap at the current tier.

items.description:
One limit's usage against its tier cap. The `current` value comes
from the matching ILimitUsageProvider registered in DI;
when no provider is registered the view reports `0` rather than
refusing to answer, because the gate is the source of truth for
enforcement and the view is read-only.

limits.description: Every registered limit, with `cap` from the tier and `current` from the matching `ILimitUsageProvider`.

version.description: Lowercase assembly version (`ComukiBuildInformation.Version`) the host boots from.

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC expiry from the verified license; `null` when `Status` is `absent`. Always present on the wire.

description:
Wire shape of `GET /api/v1/edition` — the dashboard and CLI's
read-only projection of the current license state. Anonymous by design
(the dashboard's first paint renders an upsell before sign-in), so the
endpoint is intentionally absent any permission / feature / role gates.
The response carries the live tier code and the current license
status (`valid` / `grace` / `expired` / `absent`);
DateTimeOffset? EditionView.ExpiresAt is always present on the wire — null when the
license is absent — so the property's contract (required+nullable)
matches what the OpenAPI document declares and generated zod on the
FE expects. The page projects `null` to `undefined` at the
wire→snapshot boundary and still branches on presence there.
